content: General regulatory factors (GRFs) such as Reb1, Abf1, Rap1, Mcm1, and Cbf1 play a critical role in organizing yeast chromatin by binding to specific core consensus DNA sequences. In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, ribosome biogenesis involves the coordinated regulation of over 200 Ribi genes, which respond to nutrient availability and cellular growth rates. Two cis-acting elements, PAC and RRPE, mediate the repression of Ribi genes during nutritional downshifts. Promoters of Ribi genes also contain binding sites for GRFs, most commonly Abf1 and Reb1, which are enriched at these promoters in vivo. The association of Abf1, Reb1, and Tbf1 with Ribi promoters is essential for full Ribi gene expression under nutrient-rich conditions and for modulating expression during glucose starvation. This modulation is characterized by a rapid decrease in expression followed by a gradual recovery. Interestingly, this response does not involve changes in Abf1 occupancy but is accompanied by a transient increase and subsequent decrease in the occupancy of the Rpd3L histone deacetylase complex. Disruption of Abf1 binding sites abolishes the recruitment of the Rpd3L complex during starvation. Mutational analysis of the DBP7 promoter highlights a complex interplay between Tbf1 sites, PAC, and RRPE elements in regulating Ribi gene transcription. GRFs thus serve as multifaceted regulators of Ribi gene expression during both exponential growth and repressive conditions. The consensus sequence for Abf1, CGTNNNNN(A/G)(C/T)GA(C/T), is found on both sides of the A1BG gene but only in distal promoters. Analysis of random datasets revealed sequences in the UTR, core promoter, and distal promoter for the negative direction, and in the distal promoter for the positive direction. The real consensus sequence yielded three results: one in the negative direction and two in the positive direction, all in distal promoters. Random sequences occurred in the UTR, proximal promoter, and distal promoter for the negative direction, and in the distal promoter for the positive direction. Although the differences between real and random sequences are small, the real sequences are likely significant, as the random datasets should have encompassed the real sequences but did not. The consensus sequence for Cbf1, TCACGTGA, did not yield any results in either real or random datasets. For Mcm1, neither of the consensus sequences TT(A/T)CCNN(A/T)TNGG(A/T)AA nor TTNCCNNNTNNGGNAA produced any results in real or random datasets. The Rap1 motif ACCCRNRCA did not yield any real results. However, testing this motif and its inverse complement using random datasets produced five consensus sequence results and four inverse complements. Two of these were located in the UTR of A1BG in the negative direction, one in the proximal promoter in the positive direction, and the remaining five in distal promoters. A reduced consensus sequence, (A/G)(A/C)ACCC(A/G)N(A/G)C(A/C)(C/T)(A/C), yielded one result in the positive direction at position 1807, less than halfway from ZNF497. Random datasets produced one result for this reduced consensus sequence and its inverse complement, both in the distal promoter closer to the zinc finger than A1BG. The occurrence of one random result per ten datasets suggests that such results are rarely random, and the real occurrences are likely active regulatory responses. The full consensus sequence C(A/C/G)(A/C/G)(A/G)(C/G/T)C(A/C/T)(A/G/T)(C/G/T)(A/G/T)(A/C/G)(A/C)(A/C/T)(A/C/T) produced four to six results in the UTR in the negative direction, one in the core promoter in the positive direction, two in the proximal promoter in the negative direction, and one in the positive direction. In the distal promoter, each direction had eight to nine results. In contrast, random datasets produced fewer results, suggesting that most real results are likely functional rather than random. The Reb1 consensus sequence TTACCC(G/T) occurs three times in A1BG: once in the UTR at position 3661 and twice in distal promoters at positions 3170 and 2912 in the positive direction, all more than halfway from either zinc finger. Random datasets produced three sequences in the UTR, one in the core promoter, one in the proximal promoter, and four to five in distal promoters. The extended Reb1 consensus sequence ATTACCCGAA did not occur in either real or random datasets. The Tbf1 consensus sequence ARCCCTAA occurs three times around A1BG: once in the negative direction within the UTR (inverse complement TTAGGGTT at position 3978) and twice in the positive direction (negative strand TTAGGGCT at position 2768 and positive strand AACCCTAA at position 2545). Both are closer to A1BG than either zinc finger. In random datasets, only inverse complements occurred in one dataset: TTAGGGCT at position 3616 and TTAGGGTT at position 198, both in the positive direction within the distal promoter.
